title: Template‑Driven Forms Basics 🏗️
description: Create forms using ngModel, ngForm, and two‑way binding.

slides.title: The Building Blocks 🧱
slides.content:
# `ngForm` and `ngModel`

Template‑driven forms rely on two main directives:
* **`ngForm`** – automatically applied to every `<form>` element; creates a top‑level `FormGroup` implicitly.
* **`ngModel`** – used with `[(ngModel)]` for two‑way data binding, plus it registers the control with the parent `ngForm`.

You just need to import `FormsModule` and start writing HTML.

quizData.question: Which directive creates the form’s FormGroup implicitly?
quizData.explanation: `ngForm` is automatically attached to `<form>` elements and creates the root FormGroup.

slides.title: The `name` Attribute is Crucial 🏷️
slides.content:
In template‑driven forms, every control must have a `name` attribute. It acts as the key in the form’s value object.

Without `name`, Angular cannot register the control and you’ll get a runtime error.

```html
<input [(ngModel)]="email" name="email">  <!-- ✅ -->
<input [(ngModel)]="email">              <!-- ❌ No name! -->
```

slides.title: Accessing Form State
slides.content: You can get the form’s values, validity, and other properties through the template reference `#loginForm="ngForm"`.

slides.title: Pro Tip 🚀
slides.content:
## Use the `json` pipe for debugging

`{{ form.value | json }}` instantly shows the whole form model. Great during development.

slides.title: Forget `name`? ⚠️
slides.content: If you omit `name`, Angular will not throw an error in the console immediately, but the form will not include that control. Always add `name` to inputs with `ngModel`.
